story.text: Moo pops his head out from behind a bench, a leaf still stuck to his horn.
Ah, Junior Detective! You’re here! I’ve been practicing my 'squirrel-speak' to go undercover. Ahem... Squeak, squeaky, squeaken?
Hazel trots over, rolling her eyes.
He’s been saying ‘My trousers are full of nuts’ for ten minutes. We’re going to need your brains on this one. Welcome to the team.

introStory.text: You arrive at the grand entrance to Pittencrieff Park, but something is wrong. The air, usually filled with birdsong and laughter, is thick with tension.
A squirrel high in a chestnut tree glares down at you, chittering suspiciously.
Further down the path, a peacock fans its tail, not in a proud display, but like a warrior raising a shield. The park is on a knife’s edge.
Suddenly, a soft ‘Hoo-hoo!’ echoes from the direction of the ancient stone ruins of Malcolm Canmore's Tower. A large tawny owl swoops down, landing silently on a low wall.
Greetings, Detectives. I thank you for coming. The very soul of our park is at stake. Someone is pulling the strings, turning friend against friend. You must discover who it is.
He gestures with a wing towards a piece of bark with names and places neatly etched into it.
Here are the key players and the disputed territories. Find the truth, and restore the peace.

revealStory.text: You’ve done it. You’ve crossed the last innocent suspect off the list. Hazel looks at your completed notes, her tail still.
That's it. There’s only one suspect left… Beatrice Bumble. And only one location we haven’t cleared… The Glasshouses.
She looks up at you, her eyes gleaming with the thrill of the final chase.
That must be it. The Queen Bee. And the hidden stash. Let’s go.
You and the team race to the Glasshouses. Inside, the air is warm and thick with the scent of tropical flowers.

High in the metal rafters, you see it: a huge, humming nest. And there, guarding a massive pile of acorns, is the mastermind herself, Beatrice ‘Bea’ Bumble, flanked by two of her biggest bee soldiers.
Bea faces you, calm and commanding.
So. The great Detective has solved my little puzzle.
But why, Bea? Why start a war?
War? This wasn’t war. It was… re-structuring. The squirrels are wasteful, burying acorns and forgetting them. The peacocks are frivolous. I brought order. Efficiency.
She gestures to the towering acorn stash.
I stole them to create a centrally controlled food supply, for the good of the park. My park.
Just then, Professor Hoot swoops in, followed by a flustered General Scramble-nut.
Your reign of terror is over, Bea!
The giant stash of acorns is returned to the squirrels. The feud is officially over.
Bea is placed under ‘hive arrest’ for the winter and her hive is tasked with extra pollination duties for a year to make up for the chaos.
Professor Hoot announces that, thanks to your investigation bringing everyone together, the first Great Glen Park Council will be formed to ensure peace for all time.
You did it, Detective. You looked past the chaos and found the truth. You have brought peace to our park.
You’re the bee’s knees, Detective!
For the first time all day, a real, genuine smile spreads across Hazel’s face. She gives you a knowing wink.
The Great Glen Feud was over.
